editorial_note: Direct Stacks Definition 9.2.1 and Stacks Section 10.2 ring convention. Exclude zero ring; invertibility requires two-sided product equal to 1.
text: A field is a nonzero commutative ring k with a multiplicative identity in which each element other than zero is a unit. Equivalently the nonzero elements form an abelian group under multiplication.

context: Stacks 4.2.8, ordinary strict functor of small categories
editorial_note: Direct Stacks Definition 4.2.8. Contravariant functors reverse arrows and are separately sourced elsewhere; do not confuse functors and pseudofunctors.
text: For categories A and B, a covariant functor F:A→B assigns each object x an object F(x) and every arrow f:x→y an arrow F(f):F(x)→F(y). It preserves identities and composition: F(id_x)=id_{F(x)} and F(g∘f)=F(g)∘F(f).

context: Stacks 4.2.5, ordinary groupoid as small category
editorial_note: Direct Stacks Definition 4.2.5, following Definitions 4.2.1 and 4.2.4. Not the same as a single-object groupoid or an abelian group.
text: A groupoid is a category in which every arrow has a two-sided inverse under composition, hence every morphism is an isomorphism. It need not have only one object, or only one arrow between objects.

context: Stacks 4.29.5: ordinary source category and strict target 2-category; invertible coherence 2-cells
editorial_note: Direct Stacks Definition 4.29.5. Pseudofunctor is NOT the same as a strict functor; record invertible unit, composition and coherence data. Base A is an ordinary category, target C is a strict 2-category under Stacks conventions.
text: A pseudofunctor P:A→C into a 2-category assigns objects and 1-morphisms as a functor would, but has invertible unit and composition comparison 2-morphisms instead of strict equality. The comparisons satisfy the identity compatibility laws and the associativity coherence equation for triples of composable arrows.
